target_customer: US healthcare organizations, payers and digital health companies with messy claims and clinical data
problem: Healthcare data is messy and inconsistent, which blocks scalable data products and analytics.
business_model: Open source core with paid enterprise applications, forward deployed engineering and support
product_category: Open source healthcare data transformation platform

founders.name: Aaron Neiderhiser
founders.background_notes: YC page says both founders are former senior execs from Health Catalyst and Strive Health.

founders.name: Coco Zuloaga
founders.background_notes: YC page: data science leader, formerly a mathematician and physicist in high-performance scientific computation.

competitors.name: OHDSI
competitors.what: Open source observational health data standard, named by the Tuva Project as its closest analogue
competitors.traction_then: Existed much longer per Tuva's writing

technical_complexity.rationale: A common data model, terminology sets and quality tests over claims data inside warehouses is detailed domain engineering rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: An open standard with community adoption (2,500+ community members, 150+ organizations claimed) creates pull, but open source also lets others copy it.

market_need_then: YC page says the first customer paid $10K per month by early 2022, and the founders argued data transformation and quality is the core healthcare data problem.

branding.domain_note: Uses tuvahealth.com; the open source project lives at thetuvaproject.com.
branding.brand_signature: The Tuva Project open source brand and a published manifesto

rebrands.why: A GitHub issue says the repo should be called Tuva while the Tuva Project names the whole community

branding.community_and_virality: Company site claims a community of 2,500+ members.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable open source brand with a manifesto and community, but the name shares words with the unrelated Project Tuva and the Tuva region, so naming origin is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Tuva won early credibility with a paying first customer and an open source project, then raised a $5M seed in December 2024 and a MultiCare investment in February 2025. Founder healthcare data experience and community adoption look like the main drivers; no Series A or exit has been found.
notes: Seed of $5M is reported by Fierce Healthcare, BusinessWire and HIT Consultant (Fierce page returned 403 on fetch; details from search snippets). The MultiCare investment amount is not stated; one snippet says total funding reached $6M, not recorded as a computed amount. Prospeo lists a $500K pre-seed in Apr 2022, single aggregator, unverified. Education not found. OHDSI source is undated.
